newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW sets recall for 12,000 Sharon minivans.
newsitem.headline: VW sets recall for 12,000 Sharon minivans.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Thursday it was launching a recall for 12,000 of its Sharon minivans.

VW said the recall action is needed to replace a part in the five point seatbelt for a child's seat. The carmaker said seats with a three-point belt are not affected in the Sharon, which was first produced in June 1995.

VW said the problem was uncovered by the carmaker and that there were no complaints from customers. VW said the repairs would be made free of charge and that customers would be notified in the coming days.

The recall is for vehicles sold throughout Europe and affects the SEAT Alhambra and Ford Galaxy versions of the vehicle, which is produced in Portugual under a joint venture between VW and Ford Motor Co.
